html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SDK: software development kit; API: application programming interface; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation

  • The Model Context Protocol (MCP): client and server roles, and the three server primitives
  • Authoring an MCP server, transports (stdio, HTTP), logging rules, deployment and integration
  • Agentic customization: choosing among built-in tools, custom tools, Skills and MCP

2MCP Server Development

Running case

Tidewater Shares Its Policy System

  • Three Claude applications need the same policy lookup: the claims assistant, a Claude Code workflow for engineers, and an Agent SDK back-office agent
  • The policy team wants to maintain the integration in one place

Primitive What it is Example
Tools Functions the model can call (with user or host approval) get_policy, create_payment_request
Resources File-like data that clients can read A policy PDF, a schema, an API response
Prompts Pre-written templates that help users do a task "Review a claim" template
  • Roles: the host (the application) runs an MCP client that connects to MCP servers. A server wraps an external system once, and any MCP-capable application can use it.
  • Authoring: use an official SDK (for example Python or TypeScript); tool definitions can be generated from type hints and docstrings (a decorator such as @mcp.tool()); then run the server with a transport.
mcp = FastMCP("tidewater-policy")

@mcp.tool()
async def get_policy(policy_number: str) -> str:
    """Return coverage limits, deductible and status for ONE policy (format TW-204518)."""
    ...

mcp.run(transport="stdio")

Transports and logging

Transport How it works Use for
stdio The client launches the server as a local subprocess and exchanges JSON-RPC messages over stdin and stdout Local tools for one user or machine
HTTP (streamable HTTP) The server runs as a network service; clients connect over HTTP Remote, shared, independently deployed servers
  • Never write to stdout in a stdio server. Standard output carries the protocol messages, so a stray print() corrupts them and breaks the server. Log to stderr (or a file) with a logging library.

Deploying and integrating

  • Claude Code: add servers in project .mcp.json (shared) or user configuration, with credentials from environment variables; local servers use stdio, remote ones HTTP.
  • Your own applications: use an MCP client library or the platform's MCP support to discover the server's tools and pass them to the model.
  • Share and maintain once: a server fixes the integration problem for many applications; version it and test its tools like any API.
Exam tip

A capability needed by several Claude applications and maintained independently is an MCP server. A print() in a stdio server breaks it: log to stderr.

Exam tip

Ask what is missing: access (tool or MCP), a procedure (Skill) or a common operation (built-in tool).

3Agentic Customization: Which Mechanism?

Mechanism What it is Choose it when Trade-off
Built-in tools Provided by the platform (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, web tools) The need is common: files, shell, search, web Nothing to build; limited to what is provided
Custom tools Functions you define and run in one application App-specific logic with tight control You build, test and run them; not reusable elsewhere
Skills Folders with instructions, and optional scripts and resources, loaded on demand Procedures and expertise (a review checklist, a report format, a workflow) Teaches how, does not give new access; progressive loading keeps context small
MCP servers Shared, independently maintained servers exposing tools, resources and prompts A capability many applications need, or an external system to integrate More to deploy and secure; extra connection and tool-definition context

How Skills load (progressive disclosure)

  1. Metadata (name and description) is always loaded so Claude knows the Skill exists and when to use it.
  2. The instructions (SKILL.md body) are loaded when the Skill is triggered.
  3. Resources and scripts are loaded only as needed; scripts run through the shell, so their code does not enter the context.

  • Combine them: an MCP server gives access, a Skill gives the procedure for using it well, and built-in tools cover the common steps.
Exam tip

Ask what is missing: access to a system (tool or MCP), knowledge of a procedure (Skill), or a common operation (built-in tool). Pick the mechanism that supplies exactly that.

4Exam Q&A

S1Three Claude applications need the same internal HR lookup, maintained by the HR team independently. What fits best?

  • APaste HR data into every prompt
  • BCopy the lookup code into each application's system prompt
  • CAn MCP server that exposes the lookup as a shared tool
  • DA built-in tool, which can reach any internal system
Show the answer

Answer: C. MCP gives a reusable integration that the HR team can maintain independently for every application.

S2An MCP stdio server stops working after a developer adds print("debug") statements. Why?

  • AThe client rejects anything that is written to stderr
  • Bstdio servers must not produce any output at all
  • CPython cannot print in servers
  • DStdout carries the protocol, so extra prints corrupt it
Show the answer

Answer: D. Stdio servers must keep stdout for protocol messages and log to stderr.

S3Which are the three primitives an MCP server can expose?

  • AModels, tokens and keys that are issued by the provider
  • BTools, resources and prompts
  • CAgents, hooks and plugins
  • DStreams, batches and caches
Show the answer

Answer: B. Servers expose tools (functions), resources (readable data) and prompts (templates).

S4A team needs Claude to follow its claim-review checklist and output format every time it is relevant, with no new system access. What fits best?

  • AA new MCP server that exposes one more tool to the model
  • BA custom billing tool
  • CA Skill that packages the procedure
  • DA larger model
Show the answer

Answer: C. Skills teach procedures and expertise on demand; they do not add access.

S5What does progressive disclosure mean for Skills?

  • ASkills load only after the model runs into errors
  • BSkills stay hidden from the model until the user asks
  • CEverything is loaded at startup into the context window
  • DMetadata always loads; instructions load when triggered; resources as needed
Show the answer

Answer: D. Staged loading keeps the context small until a Skill is needed.

S6A function is needed by one application only and must run entirely in that application's code. Which mechanism fits?

  • AA built-in tool that the platform provides to every application
  • BA custom tool defined in that application
  • CAn MCP server for the whole company, run by a separate team
  • DA Skill
Show the answer

Answer: B. App-specific logic belongs in a custom tool unless reuse justifies a server.

S7Which TWO statements about MCP transports are correct? Select TWO.

  • AA remote shared server is typically reached over HTTP
  • Bstdio servers should log to stdout
  • CHTTP servers cannot expose tools
  • DA stdio server runs as a local subprocess and communicates over stdin and stdout
  • ETransports change which primitives exist
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. Local servers use stdio and remote ones use HTTP; stdio logs belong on stderr.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
MCP roles Host with MCP client ↔ MCP server
Primitives Tools (functions) · resources (readable data) · prompts (templates)
Authoring Official SDKs; tools from type hints and docstrings; mcp.run(transport="stdio")
Transports stdio (local subprocess, JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout) · HTTP (remote service)
Logging Never stdout in stdio servers; log to stderr
Integrate .mcp.json (project) or user config; credentials from env vars
Choose Built-in = common ops · custom tool = one app · Skill = procedure · MCP = shared external capability
Skills Metadata always · SKILL.md when triggered · resources and scripts as needed
